rows.verdict: REFUTED AS STATED, CORRECTED AND CONFIRMED
rows.predicted: K1 sector factors are POSITIVE RATIONAL INTEGERS, rate 1.000
rows.measured: they are rational integers only in degenerate small instances (p=17: n_0 = p-1; p=641 linear); at p=97/193 the rate is 0.005-0.011. The CORRECT exact statement is: the K1 sector factor equals prod over antipodal pairs of (2 + zeta^s + zeta^{-s}) EXACTLY, hence is a TOTALLY POSITIVE real cyclotomic integer. Measured rate of that identity: 1.000 on both sectors at p = 17, 97, 193, 641 (C1p; V3: 470 K1 frequencies, 0 violations).
rows.note: self-caught over-strong pre-registration; the corrected form is stronger structurally (an exact normal form, not just a sign)

Contrast: G frequencies give fixed-sector flat 0.63-0.72 and all-even rate 0.000-0.050.

rows.predicted: the {K1 and trivial fixed-sector shadow} class is non-empty and there the fixed factor is exactly 2^{n_0}
rows.measured: non-empty at every instance; for the linear character it is exactly the trace-zero line {c = b w}, density (p-1)/(p^2-1) = 1/(p+1) (16/288 exhaustive at p=17; 35, 21, 9 hits in 4000-frequency samples at p = 97, 193, 641). Fixed factor = 2^{n_0} exactly in every case (V6, 28 frequencies). Its b-resolved contraction is 0.000 bits at every b, in BOTH currencies (C4).

rows.predicted: class mean of exp(S_c) per antipodal pair -> 2.000 on K1 and 1.6211 on G
rows.measured: the PER-ELEMENT constants are exact: (1/p) sum_s (2 + 2 cos(2 pi s/p)) = 2.00000 exactly (parity-pure pairs), (1/p) sum_s |2 cos(pi s/p)| = 1.27505/1.27330/1.27325 -> 4/pi = 1.27324 (generic), square 1.6212. The PRODUCT-level class mean is heavy-tailed: exhaustive linear-class (all K1) means per pair 1.7434 (p=17), 1.9791 (p=97), 2.2162 (p=193, 20k sample); sampled G means 2.33/1.91/1.70 are not reliable at these sizes. The 2^{n/2} vs (4/pi)^n statement is therefore banked as a FIRST-MOMENT HEURISTIC with exact per-element input, not as a measurement.

rows.measured: K1 rows: fixed/moving/total all-coefficients-real = 1/1/1 at every case (C4); G rows: 0/0/0. K2 rows: 0/0/0 (K2 factors are squares, real only at z = 1) -- outside P7's scope, recorded.
j* = 8 exactly; ratio = 762.03 (1/43 budget) and 10922.50 (1/3 budget). Exact integers, no model.

rows.predicted: the fixed sector is not structurally better than an equal-size moving window at K1
rows.measured: worst-central-band bits at rung-1 scale (equal sector sizes): fixed/moving = 10.830/10.830 (p=17 linear), 19.892/18.476 (p=97 linear), 7.235/11.473 and 17.625/13.842 (multi) -- ratio in [0.63, 1.27], never a structural advantage; 0.000/18.476 on the trivial-shadow sub-class. In the lane's carry currency both sectors saturate at exactly log2 p.

falsifiers.F1: FIRES. The parity-pure class is absorbed by nothing banked: the fixed sector is in the identical degenerate class (P3), supplies no sign (P1/P2), enters a rung only through the base offset (C7), is 2^-16 of the group (P8), and on a non-empty sub-class the fixed-sector theorem's own non-vacuity hypothesis fails outright (P5).
falsifiers.F2: FIRES. Exact per-rung arithmetic: total 1/43 deficit 1.278482e10 bits vs fixed-sector capacity 2^24 = 1.6777e7 bits (762.03x); a SINGLE rung's deficit exceeds the entire fixed-sector capacity from rung 8 on.
